p: With deterministic inference enabled and 64 output tokens, the selected schedule passes 9/9 batch/context comparisons against unmodified EAGLE3 (136 timed sequences). Batch 1 uses the ordinary EAGLE fallback. The batch-5 case exercises an uneven split. The long-context cases use the explicitly approved draft position-cache extension.

Target-only versus unmodified EAGLE3 already differs at zero-based token 13 for B1/4k, before applying the new schedule, while each mode is repeatable. This experiment does not establish target-only bit-exactness for EAGLE3; the cause of that baseline difference is not isolated. The final long-context checks above retain any additional mismatches instead of aborting before testing the new schedule.

The four main serving modes each score 19/20 on the same short-context GSM8K sanity sample. This is a small smoke test, not a quality estimate for 16k–128k extrapolation. The rejected PDL variant also scores 19/20 despite unstable token outputs, which is why its timing is excluded from valid speedup claims.

The final targeted CPU regression suites pass 22 tests plus 27 subtests, including nested profiler attribution and microbatch snapshot/restore contracts. Two-rank synthetic graph checks verify exact output equality and kernel-attribute preservation with 1/2/4/8 compute groups in serial and overlap modes. Pre-commit checks pass. All measured throughput cells separately validate complete 128-token outputs, identical prompt hashes across modes, no retractions, and graph replay at the requested profiled batch.
